units.translation: I turn aside to the worse part
Having turned aside, the Erinys brought about the bitter end of the marriage
For the shameful, wretched, first-destructive madness emboldens mortals
Do you thus torment the wretched, distracted woman with goad-driven fear?
Of one who wanders in mind

in a part of the play lost from M. Thus I corrected the corrupt reading ἢ κάρτ᾽ ἄρ᾽ ἂν παρεσκόπεις χρησμῶν ἐμῶν [or truly then you would have overlooked my oracles], with Meineke leading the way, Philol. vol. 19 p. 209, who had conjectured ἢ κάρτα τἄρ᾽ αὖ παρεκόπης χρησμῶν ἐμῶν [or truly then again you were deceived of my oracles] after Hartung, who had edited ή κάρτα τἄρα παρεκόπης χρησμῶν ἐμῶν [or truly then you were deceived of my oracles]. In the copies Flor. and Ven. ει [ei] is written over ης [ēs], i.e. παρεσκόπεις [you were overlooking], which is a word foreign to this passage, and if Aeschylus had wanted to use it, he would not have made a verse so unskillfully composed, when it was easy to write ή κάρτα χρησμῶν ὅρον ἐμῶν παρεσκόπεις [or truly you were overlooking the boundary of my oracles], which I conjectured in the Oxford edition p. 409, with Musgrave leading the way, who had conjectured κάρθ᾽ ὅρον παρεσκόπεις χρησμῶν ἐμῶν [you were overlooking the boundary of my oracles], better than Canter, who had wanted ἢ κάρτ᾽ ἀράν [or truly a curse], which does not suit the preceding words where there is no mention of curses. A passive aorist of another verb is required, of which a trace is left in the corrupt reading παρεσκόπης [you were deceived], and ἄρ᾽ ἂν [then would] is the supplement of a corrector filling in the missing foot, which I accomplished by adding κλύων [hearing]. The same participle had fallen out at the end of the verse Sept. 394, where μένων [remaining] was introduced, which was made from μένει [he remains], with which the preceding verse ends.
Or truly you were deceived, hearing my oracles
or truly then would you have overlooked my oracles
or truly then again you were deceived of my oracles
or truly then you were deceived of my oracles
or truly you were overlooking the boundary of my oracles
you were overlooking the boundary of my oracles
thus without accent, corrupt from πάρος [before], which Sophianus restored, Suppl. 368.
For other examples of the feminine termination see Thes. vol. 6 p. 305.
In the plural number παραλλαγαί [alternations] the turns of those succeeding each other in turn.
the alternations of light-bearing torches, beacon-fires and fire
